subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Threshold is a 2019 stained glass artwork by British artist Ivy Dalton.
• It is a large panel depicting abstract geometric shapes in cobalt and amber.
• Stained glass became widespread in European cathedrals in the 12th century and declined in ecclesiastical use after the 17th century.
• Stained glass was embraced by fine artists in the mid-20th century and continues to be a popular artistic medium today.
• Curator Patrick Sullivan says, "[Stained glass] demands that each piece be cut and leaded by hand, since the craft resists industrial shortcuts."
prompt: The student wants to connect the artwork to the history of stained glass in art. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Threshold, like other stained glass works, must, as Sullivan notes, be cut and leaded by hand, since the craft resists any industrial shortcuts.
choices.B: With Threshold, Dalton joins the decades-long lineage of fine artists who have helped make stained glass a popular artistic medium since the mid-20th century.
choices.C: From the 12th century to today, stained glass has remained a popular material, serving both as a feature of cathedrals and as an artistic medium.
choices.D: The cobalt and amber panel Threshold pays tribute to the rich tradition of a medium whose artistic popularity has long been in decline.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The sentence effectively connects the artwork Threshold to the history of stained glass in art, noting that Dalton's 2019 work joins the decades-long tradition of fine artists who have made stained glass a popular artistic medium since the mid-20th century.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The sentence misrepresents information from the notes by suggesting that stained glass has been continuously popular in ecclesiastical use from the 12th century to today, when the notes indicate that its ecclesiastical use declined after the 17th century. Additionally, it doesn't specifically connect Threshold to the artistic history of stained glass.
